# Subsetting Astrocytes from All Celltype-Seurat

This is the first script of this project. In this project, I analysed single-
nuclei RNA sequencing (snRNAseq) data of post-mortem spinal cord tissue of 20
ALS patients and 4 controls, focusing on astrocytes. In this script, I will open
the full dataset (with all celltypes), examine the astrocytes (e.g. what 
proportion of total cells they form per sample), and subset the astrocytes.

``` {r 01_setup, include = FALSE} 
# Manage settings for code chunks throughout the document
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

# Prerequisites

This script was run with the *conda environment* `r_scrnaseq_core`.

``` {r 02_packages_directories}
##  Open packages --------------------------------------------------------------

library(Seurat)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)


##  Set directories ------------------------------------------------------------


# Now forms a hardcoded 'bug' - I will fix this later, using the package here
dir_home <- "/hpc/hers_en/nboersbroek/projects/snrna_astros_shortread_postQC"

# Data directories
dir_data <- file.path(dir_home, "data/raw")

# Results directories
dir_fig <- file.path(dir_home, "results/figures/01_subsetting_astros")
dir.create(dir_fig, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = TRUE)
```

## Helper functions

### save_plot()

This document will display all images I make. However, I also want to save these images on disk - both as a .pdf file and .png file. This function saves both; I only need to provide the ggplot-object, the name for the file (without filetype extension!) and optionally the width and heigth of the figure. 
``` {r xx_helpers}
# file.path provides the path, but I need to use paste0 to concatenate .png
save_plot <- function(p, filename, width = 10, height = 6) {
  png_file <- file.path(dir_fig, paste0(filename, ".png"))
  ggsave(png_file, p, width = width, height = height, dpi = 150)
  pdf_file <- file.path(dir_fig, paste0(filename, ".pdf"))
  ggsave(pdf_file, p, width = width, height = height, dpi = 150)
}
```

## Defining variables

This code block defines variables to be used throughout the rest of the
document. Users can adapt these if desired.

``` {r, 02_defining variables}
astro_markers <- c("GFAP", "AQP4", "SLC1A2", "OBI1-AS1")
```

# Astrocytes in the dataset with all celltypes

## Load Seurat in from disk

The object `seu_spinal_allcelltypes_shortread_postQC.rds` was the object which 
Charlotte shared with me after her full QC.

``` {r 03_open_seurat}
file_rds <- paste0(dir_data, "seu_spinal_allcelltypes_shortread_postQC.rds")
seu <- readRDS(file_rds)
# Test whether it loaded in correctly
seu
```

## Visualization annotation all celltypes

Charlotte defined major cell types using a publicly available atlas of the human
spinal cord of the Allan Brain Insitute. These are stored in the columns 
`predicted.id_coarse_allen_subclass` and `predicted.id_coarse_allen_group`,
with the latter having a more subdivided annotation than the former.

``` {r 04_umap_subclass}
# I want to show both subclass and cellclass. First show subclass
p_allen_subclass <- DimPlot(
  seu,
  reduction = "umap",
  group.by = "predicted.id_coarse_allen_Subclass",
  label = TRUE,
  repel = TRUE
) +
  NoLegend() +
  ggtitle("UMAP after filtering - Allen subclass")
p_allen_subclass
```

``` {r 05_umap_cellclass}
p_allen_group <- DimPlot(
  seu,
  reduction = "umap",
  group.by = "predicted.id_coarse_allen_group",
  label = TRUE,
  repel = TRUE
) +
  NoLegend() +
  ggtitle("UMAP after filtering - Allen Group")
p_allen_group
```

```{r 06_save_plots, echo = FALSE}
# Store the plots, but keep this hidden for the output
save_plot(p_allen_subclass, "allcelltypes_umap_alansubclass")
save_plot(p_allen_group, "allcelltypes_umap_alangroup")
```

## Visualization astrocyte markers

I previously provided the annotation of celltypes, but I would like to confirm
that the labelled astrocytes are astrocytes. A FeaturePlot() with 
astrocyte-marker genes forms a quick way to do so. In the default settings of 
this document, I provided the astrocyte marker genes 
`c("GFAP", "AQP4", "SLC1A2", "OBI1-AS1")`. You can see that the astrocyte cluster
expresses these markers.

``` {r 07_featureplot}
p_feature <- FeaturePlot(
  seu,
  features = astro_markers,
  reduction = "umap"
)
p_feature
```

```{r 08_save_plots, echo = FALSE}
# Store the plot, but keep this hidden for the output
save_plot(p_feature, "allcelltypes_featureplot")
```

## Visualization astrocyte frequency

I want to show how many astrocytes each sample has. I will show both the
absolute frequency and the relative frequency.

``` {r 09_preprocessing_freq}
# Create a dataframe which contains the count of astrocyte- and
# non-astrocyte-cells of each participant
metadata <- seu@meta.data |>
  as.data.frame()
# Make a Boolean-like astrocyte-non-astrocyte column
metadata$astro <- ifelse(
  test = metadata$predicted.id_coarse_allen_subclass == "Astrocytes",
  yes = "Astrocyte",
  no = "Non-Astrocyte"
)
freq_table <- table(
  metadata$astro,
  metadata$AnonymousID
) |>
  as.data.frame()
colnames(freq_table) <- c("Celltype", "Sample", "Frequency")

# The levels aren't ordered like I want: it's in the order ALS1, ALS10, ALS11,
# ..., ALS19, ALS2, ALS20, ALS3, ALS4 etc. etc. It does not count up from
# ALS1 to ALS 9 and then from 10 to 20, becuase ALS1 till ALS 9 is in single
# digits... I tried to fix it with this ugly fix, but it did not work; I'll
# leave it for now
freq_table <- freq_table |>
  mutate(
    Sample = fct_relevel(
      Sample,
      "ALS1", "ALS2", "ALS3", "ALS4", "ALS5", "ALS6", "ALS7", "ALS8", "ALS9"
    )
  )

# Inspect what this dataframe looks like
kable(head(freq_table))
```

``` {r 10_absolute_freq}
p_abs <- ggplot(freq_table, aes(fill = Celltype, y = Frequency, x = Sample)) +
  geom_bar(position = "stack", stat = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#EF2400", "grey")) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) # otherwise unreadable x-axis
p_abs
```

``` {r 11_proportional_freq}
p_prop <- ggplot(freq_table, aes(fill = Celltype, y = Frequency, x = Sample)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill", stat = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#EF2400", "grey")) + # red-grey = easy to read
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))
p_prop
```

```{r 12_save_plots, echo = FALSE}
# Store the plot, but keep this hidden for the output
save_plot(p_abs, "allcelltypes_barplot_abs")
save_plot(p_prop, "allcelltypes_barplot_prop")
```

# Subset astrocytes and save on disk

Now that we have inspected the astrocytes in the whole dataset, I can subset
the astrocytes which I will continue in the rest of the project. I wil subset
the astrocytes as annotated in the column `predicted.id_coarse_allen_subclass`, 
which was visualized in the first image under the header 
**Visualization annotation all celltypes**.

``` {r 13_subset_astros}
seu_astros <- subset(
  seu,
  subset = predicted.id_coarse_allen_subclass == "Astrocytes"
)
# Inspect
seu_astros
```

Even though one could technically call this preprocessed, I will still store
this subsetted astrocyte file in the folder `data/raw`; it's still a raw Seurat
object without preprocessing, but  now it's just astrocytes.

``` {r 14_save_to_disk}
file_rds <- paste0(dir_data, "seu_spinal_astros_shortread_postQC.rds")
saveRDS(seu_astros, file_rds)
```
